tabs.title: Company Overview
tabs.content:
**Traversia Rail** operates passenger and freight rail services across three countries. Its ticketing platform runs in Microsoft Azure, its real-time freight tracking system runs in Amazon Web Services (AWS) after an acquisition, and signaling support systems remain in company data centers.

**Current Environment:**
- The security operations team is three analysts who cover business hours only.
- Security posture is reviewed ad hoc: the Azure estate has some oversight, but nobody assesses the AWS accounts against any security standard.
- Logs from the ticketing platform, the AWS freight system, station networks, and third-party badge readers sit in separate consoles and are only examined after something goes wrong.

tabs.title: Security Program Objectives
tabs.content:
The newly appointed head of security at Traversia Rail has set these objectives:
- **One posture view**: Bring the Azure subscriptions *and* the AWS accounts under a single tool that continuously assesses configuration against security standards and recommends hardening steps.
- **Centralize the signal**: Aggregate and correlate log data from cloud platforms, on-premises systems, and third-party devices in one analytics platform so threats are detected from combined evidence, not single consoles.
- **Get ahead of alerts**: Give analysts a way to proactively search the collected data for signs of compromise that no alert has fired for, based on hypotheses from recent threat reports.
